summary: Defines a DHCPv6 option carrying IPv6 prefixes used to build IPv4-embedded unicast and multicast addresses for multicast IPv4 service continuity.

eli5.summary: A device is told which prefix to use to wrap old addresses into new ones.

questions: what is an ipv4-embedded ipv6 address
how are ipv4 multicast addresses mapped to ipv6
subtitle: A DHCPv6 option that tells a device which IPv6 prefixes to use when wrapping IPv4 addresses for multicast transition.

tldr.problem: IPv4 multicast delivery over IPv6 networks uses special IPv6 addresses that embed IPv4 addresses, and devices need a way to learn which IPv6 prefixes to build them from.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8115 defines the DHCPv6 option OPTION_V6_PREFIX64, which carries an ASM multicast prefix, an SSM multicast prefix and a unicast prefix, each used to synthesize IPv4-embedded IPv6 addresses.
tldr.outcome: A DHCPv6 client can be configured automatically with the prefixes. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 8115 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2017, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Prefix Option Is Needed
sections.content:
Several solutions, such as RFC 8114, deliver multicast services while networks move to IPv6. Even though their use cases differ, they all use special IPv6 addresses that embed IPv4 addresses, for both multicast group addresses and source addresses.

RFC 8115 defines a DHCPv6 option that carries the IPv6 prefixes used to build those IPv4-embedded IPv6 addresses. The RFC says the option can be used with Dual-Stack Lite (DS-Lite), Stateless Address plus Port (A+P) and other IPv4-IPv6 transition techniques.
sections.eli5: When old and new addresses have to share a network, devices need to know the rule for converting one into the other. This option hands them that rule.

sections.title: Prefix64 Terminology
sections.content:
An IPv4-embedded IPv6 address is an IPv6 address that embeds a 32-bit-encoded IPv4 address, as described in RFC 6052. It can be unicast or multicast. A Prefix64 is an IPv6 prefix used for synthesizing such addresses; the "64" abbreviates IPv6-IPv4 interconnection.

  • ASM_mPrefix64: a multicast Prefix64 in the Any-Source Multicast (ASM) range.
  • SSM_mPrefix64: a multicast Prefix64 in the Source-Specific Multicast (SSM) range.
  • uPrefix64: a unicast Prefix64 for building the IPv4-embedded IPv6 addresses of multicast sources in SSM mode.
sections.eli5: There are three kinds of wrapping prefixes: one for group chats anyone can join, one for group chats from a named speaker, and one for naming the speaker.

sections.title: The OPTION_V6_PREFIX64 Option
sections.content:
The option holds an option code, an option-length in octets, and three length-and-prefix pairs: asm-length with ASM_mPrefix64, ssm-length with SSM_mPrefix64, and unicast-length with uPrefix64. Each length field is an 8-bit unsigned integer giving the number of valid leading bits in the prefix.

asm-length and ssm-length MUST be set to 96, and the conveyed multicast prefixes MUST belong to the ASM and SSM ranges respectively. unicast-length MUST be one of 32, 40, 48, 56, 64 or 96, as specified in RFC 6052. uPrefix64 is variable in size, rounded up to the nearest octet boundary, with any padding bits zeroed.

Multiple instances of the option may be returned to a client. The authors considered defining three distinct options but did not, because that would have created an option usable to discover unicast Prefix64s where multicast is not enabled. That conflicts with the recommendation to support the Well-Known DNS Name heuristic method for unicast-only environments (RFC 7051).
sections.eli5: The option is a form with three boxes: one for each kind of prefix, each with a note saying how much of the box is filled in.

sections.title: DHCPv6 Client Behavior
sections.content:
To get the prefixes, the client MUST include the OPTION_V6_PREFIX64 code in its OPTION_ORO. If it receives more than one such option and each multicast prefix has a distinct scope, the client MUST pick the prefix whose scope matches the IPv4 multicast address being converted. If at least two options carry multicast prefixes with the same scope, those options MUST be discarded.

If asm-length, ssm-length and unicast-length are all 0, the client MUST behave as if the option had not been received.

To build a multicast address, the client concatenates the ASM or SSM prefix with the IPv4 multicast address, which goes in the last 32 bits. A non-null unicast-length means uPrefix64 is used to build IPv4-embedded unicast addresses as specified in RFC 6052.
sections.eli5: The device asks for the option, picks the prefix that matches the kind of address it is converting, and sticks the old address on the end.

sections.title: Server Configuration Advice
sections.content:
Appendix A gives non-normative recommendations for DHCP servers. A server must be configured with ASM_mPrefix64 or SSM_mPrefix64, and may be configured with both, in the same option. uPrefix64 must be configured when an SSM prefix is provided, and may be configured with an ASM prefix. It is not mandatory for ASM if, for example, a local mapping algorithm is supported or the Well-Known Prefix (64:ff9b::/96) is used.

A configured multicast Prefix64 must be a /96. When distinct IPv6 multicast scopes are needed to preserve scope when translating IPv4 multicast addresses, each scope is configured as a separate option instance; otherwise only one instance is configured.
sections.eli5: The people running the network are told which boxes to fill in, depending on what kind of group traffic they support.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC adds no security text of its own. It states only that the security considerations in RFC 3315 and RFC 6052 are to be considered.
sections.eli5: The rules for staying safe are the ones already written down for the older documents, so this one points to them.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA assigned option code 113 to OPTION_V6_PREFIX64 in the DHCPv6 parameters registry.
sections.eli5: The official list of option numbers now has this option written in it at number 113.

fields.name: option-length
fields.desc: Length of the option, in octets.

fields.name: asm-length
fields.desc: Prefix length for the ASM prefix; MUST be 96.

fields.name: ASM_mPrefix64
fields.desc: Multicast prefix in the ASM range (continues past this row).

fields.name: ssm-length
fields.desc: Prefix length for the SSM prefix; MUST be 96.

fields.name: SSM_mPrefix64
fields.desc: Multicast prefix in the SSM range (continues past this row).

fields.name: uPrefix64
fields.desc: Variable-size unicast prefix (continues past this row).
